The Brand

The Pangolin.
& The Founder.

Two things make SafeRise truly special, unlike anything else in the wellness space — a brand built on the spirit animal that embodies the methodology, and a founder whose life story is the proof of concept.

The SafeRise Icon

The pangolin is nature's most armoured creature. Its only defence is not to fight or flee — but to curl inward towards its heart, protected by its own scales, completely unbreachable from within. When the threat passes, it opens — standing firm, eyes forward, feet planted. Unmoved by what surrounds. The SafeRise embodied state in nature's own design.

A percentage of every SafeRise Protocol subscription goes directly to pangolin sanctuaries in South Africa — protecting the very animal that embodies this work.

The Founder

The story is
the product.

The SafeRise Protocol did not emerge from academic study. It emerged from lived navigation — of abandonment trauma, relational patterns that repeated until they were understood, and the long process of learning to recalibrate from survival into grounded, secure presence.

The four-step Protocol was not designed in theory. It was discovered in practice, refined through repetition, and validated through the shift it produced.

When I recognised that every reactive behaviour I carried was rooted in a safety deficit — not a character flaw — everything shifted.

That recognition is what the SafeRise Protocol is built to give others.

— Andre, Founder

Andre Robley is the founder of SafeRise, a nervous-system regulation platform built on polyvagal theory, heart-brain coherence research, and Jungian shadow-work. He is trained in Jungian shadow-work frameworks, somatic coaching, and meditation practice.

Common Questions

Before You Begin

Is this therapy or clinical treatment?

No. The SafeRise Protocol is a self-regulation methodology — not therapy, not clinical treatment, and not a replacement for professional mental health support. It is a practical nervous system tool you can use in daily life, alongside any other support you are receiving.

Do I need a diagnosis or any prior experience?

No diagnosis required. No prior experience with breathwork, meditation, or therapy needed. You simply need to know what you are feeling right now. The protocols are designed to meet you exactly where you are.

How is this different from meditation apps?

Meditation apps teach you to maintain a state. The SafeRise Protocol is designed to shift you from one state to another — specifically when you are in activation, distress, or overwhelm. It works in the moments meditation is hardest to access.

I am already in therapy. Can I still use this?

Yes — and many people find the two work well together. Therapy builds long-term insight. The SafeRise Protocol gives you a tool for the moments between sessions when a trigger arrives and you need something right now.

What if I buy a module and it is not right for me?

We offer a 30-day satisfaction guarantee. If you have genuinely engaged with the content and do not feel it delivered value, contact us and we will make it right. No complicated process.

The state it's holding

Your body already
knows which one.

Pay attention to your state, not the story. Your autonomic nervous system moves across a range — and only one end of it gives you access to perspective, patience and judgement.

Mobilisation

Sympathetic

Safety

Ventral vagal · your regulated range

Shutdown

Dorsal vagal

"Everything needs handling, and it needs handling now."

Racing, bracing, scanning. Sharp with people you love. The reaction is out before you've decided anything.

"This is hard. I can deal with it."

Relief enters the body: shoulders lower, breath opens, attention returns. The hard thing remains — but you have options in front of it.

"None of it is worth the energy."

Flat, distant, unreachable — including to yourself. Not laziness. The system conserving what's left.

You already know your regulated self.

The work is learning how to return there on purpose.

Why naming it isn't enough

Understanding and integration
are two different events.

Insight arrives through language. Safety arrives through the body. You can't reason your way into a state that reasoning depends on.

First

The body protects

Your nervous system commits to a survival response in the brainstem and amygdala — before your conscious mind has processed a single word.

Then

The mind explains

In that state the higher functions you'd need are not available. Not suppressed by weakness — offline by design. Which is why one more explanation of the pattern was never going to be enough.

A trigger travels on two timelines

Regulate the fast route first.Then reflection becomes available.

You weren't holding on out of weakness.
Your system was holding on out of survival.

What reaches it instead

The Protocol Foundation.
A guided system.

A repeatable route from recognition to regulation — four actions your own system learns to run.

Step 01Step 02 Step 03Step 04

Identify & Name

Name what's actually present, specifically. Not "I feel anxious" — finish the sentence "what I'm afraid will happen is ___." Precision is itself regulating.

Porges · Polyvagal Theory

Redirect to Heart

Hand to heart. In for four, out for six — roughly six breaths a minute. The cardiac rhythm gives the nervous system physical evidence of safety that argument cannot supply.

HeartMath · Cardiac coherence

Accept & Release

Meet what's there without fighting it — including your own part in it. Set down self-blame; acceptance is the decision. Release is what the body does once it registers safe.

Maté · Compassionate Inquiry

Gratitude & Expansion

Still in coherence, rehearse the version of yourself on the other side — and let the body feel it as already true. You leave carrying the state, not just the memory of it.

Mental rehearsal · Observer stance

Step 02 · The coherence rhythm

Six breaths a minute is where heart-rate variability peaks for most people. Pacing the breath there is the most direct, measurable way to move your state — the body reads the rhythm as evidence of safety before the mind has agreed to anything.

About six breaths per minute.No force. No perfect count.

The sequence becomes familiar

Each repetition shortens the route.The body learns what comes next.

The same four steps. The same voice. A route your body can recognise.

Common Questions

Before you start.

The things worth knowing, answered plainly.

Is this therapy?

No. SafeRise is a structured self-guided practice and coaching resource, not psychotherapy, counselling, or medical treatment. Andre is trained in Jungian shadow-work frameworks, somatic coaching, and meditation practice — he is not a licensed therapist or psychiatrist, and nothing here is a diagnosis.

Many people use it alongside therapy. It is designed to give you something practical to do in the moment a pattern shows up, between the sessions where you unpack why it exists.

What if I'm already working with a therapist?

That combination tends to work well, and it's worth telling them you're doing it. Each protocol includes a Disclosure & Support script partly for this — a short way to explain what the practice involves so they can tell you whether it fits what you're working on together.

If your therapist advises against it, follow their guidance. They know your situation; a website doesn't.

Do I need experience with meditation or somatic work?

None. Every protocol is fully guided from start to finish — you're told what to do, when, and for how long. If you've tried meditation and found that being left alone with your thoughts made things worse, this is deliberately not that.

How long does a session take, and what do I need?

Around ten minutes. Headphones if you have them, somewhere you won't be interrupted, and the ability to sit or lie down. Nothing else — no journal to prepare, no prior reading.

There's also a Crisis Card in every protocol: a four-line version for moments when ten minutes isn't realistic.

Which protocol should I start with?

The one that names what you're feeling right now. That's the whole design — you don't need to work out an underlying cause first, and there's no correct order.

If nothing obviously matches, start with the Foundation Protocol. It teaches the four steps in their simplest form, and every other protocol is a variation on it.

What actually comes with a protocol?

A guided audio session, a printable step guide, the science behind the pattern, a reference case, body-based practices for between sessions, journalling prompts, and a crisis card. Some protocols also include an Attention Advisory or an Invitation to Repair where another person is genuinely part of the pattern.

You are not expected to use all of it. Most people use two or three and ignore the rest.

What can change, and how long does it take?

SafeRise does not promise that a feeling will disappear permanently, or that your history will be erased. The aim is a more familiar route back to choice when the state returns. If a method promises a feeling will never return, that is a claim about you it has no way of making.

There is no fixed timeline. Some shifts may be noticeable within a session; lasting familiarity depends on repetition and what else is happening in your life. Your tracker shows what is changing in your own experience.

Over time the aim is that you carry the sequence rather than run every step — a method that needs you permanently is designed around its own retention, not your regulation.

Can I use this while I'm actually in the middle of it?

Yes — that's what the Crisis Card is for, and it's designed to be readable when concentration is poor. The full session is better done once things have settled slightly.

If you're experiencing severe physical symptoms, or symptoms you haven't had before, treat that as a medical question first and speak to a doctor.

Is any of this based on real science?

The core of it rests on peer-reviewed work: Stephen Porges's Polyvagal Theory, the HeartMath Institute's research on heart-rhythm coherence, and Gabor Maté's Compassionate Inquiry. Carl Jung's shadow and individuation frameworks and Joe Dispenza's work on the observer state are included as interpretive layers rather than clinical evidence, and we try to be clear about which is which.

SafeRise has not been through a clinical trial. It is a structured practice built on established frameworks, not a treatment with proven outcomes.

Is my journal private?

Your entries and progress data are yours. They aren't shared, sold, or used to target advertising. Full detail is in the Privacy Policy.

What if it doesn't work for me?

Cancel any time from your account — there's no contract and no cancellation call. If it isn't landing within the first month, we'd rather you stopped than kept paying out of obligation.

Regulation practices are not universal. Some nervous systems respond faster to movement, or to another person in the room, than to a guided sequence alone.

Can I use it with a partner?

Track 01 is intrinsic work — just you and your own system. Relationship Healing is the track built for two people practising together, and it's in development.

I've tried things like this before and they didn't stick.

Understanding a pattern does not always interrupt it while it is happening. SafeRise gives you a fixed sequence to run during the state, then a way to record what changed afterwards.

That is a different practice from collecting more explanations. Repetition and your own tracking will tell you whether it is useful for you.

What if I'm in crisis right now?

SafeRise is not crisis support and shouldn't be used as a substitute for it. If you're in immediate danger, contact your local emergency number.

If you need to talk to someone now, findahelpline.com lists free, confidential helplines by country. Reaching out there is the right move, and it's not an overreaction.

Your SafeRise Protocol is ready when you are.

RelationshipHealing

Extrinsic work — you in relation to another. Ten protocols for the dynamics that keep repeating, self-paced.

Common Questions

Before you start.

The things worth knowing, answered plainly.

Is this therapy?

No. SafeRise is a structured self-guided practice and coaching resource, not psychotherapy, counselling, or medical treatment. Andre is trained in Jungian shadow-work frameworks, somatic coaching, and meditation practice — he is not a licensed therapist or psychiatrist, and nothing here is a diagnosis.

Many people use it alongside therapy. It is designed to give you something practical to do in the moment a pattern shows up, between the sessions where you unpack why it exists.

What if only one of us wants to do this?

It still works. Every protocol is written to be done by one person as easily as two — the Safety Score and Session Guide adapt to a single participant, and several protocols are specifically about what one person can shift regardless of where the other is. Doing your own half of the pattern often changes the dynamic even without them.

If you'd rather wait until you're both in, that's fine too — nothing here is timed.

Do we need experience with therapy or couples work?

None. Every protocol is fully guided from start to finish — you're both told what to do, when, and for how long. If a hard conversation has always meant winging it and hoping it goes well, this is deliberately not that.

How long does a session take, and what do we need?

Around ten minutes together. Somewhere private, both phones down, and the willingness to actually try the sequence rather than talk about trying it. Nothing else — no journal to prepare, no prior reading.

Run the Safety Score first if either of you is unsure whether this is the right moment to start.

Which protocol should we start with?

The one that names what's actually happening between you right now. That's the whole design — you don't need to agree on whose fault it is first, and there's no correct order.

If you're not sure, start with the Safe Conversation Protocol. It teaches the slow-down sequence every other protocol in this track builds on.

What actually comes with a protocol?

A guided audio session for the two of you, a Session Guide with the exact script, the science behind the pattern, a Safety Score to check in before you start, a historical reference case, and journalling prompts for after. You're not expected to use all of it every time — most couples lean on the audio and the Safety Score, and dip into the rest as needed.

Can we use this in the middle of a fight?

That's exactly what the Safety Score is for — a fast check, before anything else, on whether this is a moment to talk or a moment to separate first. If either of you answers it honestly and it says stop, stop. The full session works better once things have cooled slightly.

If there's ever a safety concern beyond an argument, treat that as urgent and act on it directly — this isn't a substitute for that.

Is any of this based on real science?

The core of it rests on peer-reviewed work: Stephen Porges's Polyvagal Theory and the HeartMath Institute's research on heart-rhythm coherence, which is where the co-regulation techniques come from. Other frameworks are included as interpretive layers rather than clinical evidence, and we try to be clear about which is which.

SafeRise has not been through a clinical trial. It is a structured practice built on established frameworks, not a treatment with proven outcomes.

Are our journal entries private from each other?

Each of you logs and journals under your own account, and entries aren't shared with your partner automatically. What you choose to say out loud to each other is up to you — the practice doesn't require reading each other's private entries to work.

What if it doesn't work for us?

Cancel any time from your account — there's no contract and no cancellation call. If it isn't landing within the first month, we'd rather you stopped than kept paying out of obligation.

Some patterns need more than a self-guided protocol can offer. That's what the live Monthly Workshop and the Premium 1:1 are for.

Do we both need our own account?

Yes — each of you tracks your own sessions and journal entries separately, even when you're doing a protocol together. That's what lets the Safety Score and progress tracking reflect where each of you actually is, not an average of the two.

What if I'm in crisis right now?

SafeRise is not crisis support and shouldn't be used as a substitute for it. If you're in immediate danger, contact your local emergency number.

If you need to talk to someone now, findahelpline.com lists free, confidential helplines by country. Reaching out there is the right move, and it's not an overreaction.

Common Questions

Before you start.

The things worth knowing, answered plainly.

Is this therapy?

No. SafeRise is a structured self-guided practice and coaching resource, not psychotherapy, counselling, or medical treatment. Andre is trained in Jungian shadow-work frameworks, somatic coaching, and meditation practice — he is not a licensed therapist or psychiatrist, and nothing here is a diagnosis.

Many people use it alongside therapy. It is designed to give you something practical to do in the moment a pattern shows up, between the sessions where you unpack why it exists.

What if I'm already working with a coach or therapist?

That combination tends to work well, and it's worth mentioning to them. Each protocol's Meditation Script is specific enough to share with a coach or therapist so they can see exactly what the practice involves and how it fits alongside what you're already doing together.

If they advise against it, follow their guidance. They know your situation; a website doesn't.

Do I need experience with meditation to use this?

None. Every protocol is fully guided from start to finish, breath-marked and word-for-word — you're told what to do, when, and for how long. If you've tried meditating before a big moment and found the silence made the spiral worse, this is deliberately not that.

How long does a session take, and what do I need?

Around ten minutes. Headphones if you have them, five minutes of actual privacy — a stairwell, a parked car, an empty meeting room — and the willingness to do it before the moment instead of just gutting it out.

The Life Companion for each protocol is built for the version of this that has to happen in under a minute, at your desk, between calls.

Which protocol should I start with?

The one that names what's actually happening for you right now — the meeting you're dreading, the burnout you're not admitting to, the idea you keep talking yourself out of. That's the whole design; there's no correct order and no need to diagnose yourself first.

If nothing obviously matches, start with the High-Stakes Presence Protocol. It teaches the core regulation sequence every other protocol in this track builds on.

What actually comes with a protocol?

A guided ten-minute meditation, a word-for-word Meditation Script, the science behind the pattern, a Life Companion for the small daily version of the practice, a reference case from a public figure who lived it, and journalling prompts. You're not expected to use all of it — most people lean on the meditation before the moment and the Life Companion between them.

Can I use this right before I walk into the room?

Yes — that's exactly what it's built for. The Life Companion is the compressed, in-the-moment version, readable in the time it takes to walk from the elevator to the door. The full ten-minute session is better done earlier, when you have the time to actually sit with it.

Is any of this based on real science?

The core of it rests on peer-reviewed work: Stephen Porges's Polyvagal Theory and the HeartMath Institute's research on heart-rhythm coherence, which is where the pre-moment regulation techniques come from. Other frameworks are included as interpretive layers rather than clinical evidence, and we try to be clear about which is which.

SafeRise has not been through a clinical trial. It is a structured practice built on established frameworks, not a treatment with proven outcomes.

Is my journal private from my employer?

Yes. Your entries and progress data are yours — they're never visible to an employer, even where a company programme is paying for access. Full detail is in the Privacy Policy.

What if it doesn't work for me?

Cancel any time from your account — there's no contract and no cancellation call. If it isn't landing within the first month, we'd rather you stopped than kept paying out of obligation.

Some pressure needs more than a self-guided protocol can offer. That's what the live Monthly Workshop and the Premium 1:1 are for.

Can my company pay for this instead of me?

Team and organisational access is handled separately from individual billing — join the waitlist above and we'll follow up about company programmes and founder pricing once this track is live.

What if I'm in crisis right now?

SafeRise is not crisis support and shouldn't be used as a substitute for it. If you're in immediate danger, contact your local emergency number.

If you need to talk to someone now, findahelpline.com lists free, confidential helplines by country. Reaching out there is the right move, and it's not an overreaction.

Premium 1:1

A private session
with the founder.

One focused hour, live, for whatever the self-guided protocols can't fully reach on their own — a specific situation, a pattern that needs a second perspective, or simply working through it with someone present. Available to any member, on any track.

What happens in the hour

You come with whatever's live for you right now — a specific moment you're stuck in, or a pattern you keep circling back to. There's no agenda to prepare, no protocol to complete beforehand.

Andre works the session live, using the same Four-Step framework behind every SafeRise protocol — Identify & Name, Redirect to Heart, Accept & Release, Gratitude & Expansion — but applied in real time to your specific situation, not a general script. You'll leave with a clear next step, not just a conversation.

Before

Nothing required. Come as you are.

During

One hour, live video, just the two of you.

After

A brief written follow-up — what came up, and where to focus next in the platform.

What Makes One Hour Enough

Undivided Focus

No group, no agenda but yours — just Andre's full attention on your specific situation.

Tailored In Real Time

The Four-Step framework applied live to what's actually happening for you, not a general script.

A Clear Next Step

You leave with something to actually do, plus a written follow-up — not just a conversation.

Why a session with Andre specifically

The protocols carry the method. This hour carries Andre's read on you — and that read draws on more than the Four-Step framework alone.

  • ◆As a trained meditation guide, Andre works with your nervous system's actual state in real time, not just the content of what you're saying — noticing where you tighten, where you go quiet, where the breath changes before you've named why.
  • ◆His grounding in somatic work means the session doesn't stay purely conversational. If a pattern lives in the body rather than the story you're telling about it, that's where the hour goes — because talking around a felt sense rarely resolves it.
  • ◆And where a pattern has real depth — something recurring, something that looks like more than a single situation — Andre draws on Jungian shadow work, the same lens behind SafeRise's Shadow Integration framework. Not analysis for its own sake, but a way of asking what a pattern is protecting, not just how to make it stop.

Together, these mean the hour can meet you wherever you actually show up — cognitive, somatic, or deeper — rather than forcing your situation into one lens because it's the only tool available.

A safe space, not a diagnosis

This isn't therapy, and it isn't a substitute for professional mental health care. It's a held, non-judgmental hour grounded in the same principles as the rest of SafeRise — nothing you say here is assessed, labeled, or judged. If something you bring needs more support than a single session can hold, Andre will tell you directly and point you toward the right kind of help.

The Four-Step Practice

01Identify & Name

Pause. Name the trigger with precision. Specificity dissolves the fog and interrupts the unconscious survival response.

02Redirect to Heart

Hand on chest. Breathe into the heart. The heart holds what the mind cannot resolve.

03Accept & Release

Acknowledge without judgment. Forgive yourself. Release resistance — it holds activation in place.

04Gratitude & Expansion

Thank your heart. Notice what changed and what that change says about who you are becoming. Name the specific identity you choose in relation to this pattern, state it as a decision rather than a hope, and take one small action that gives that identity evidence. Each cycle expands your baseline capacity — the learning compounds.

The foundation every premium protocol is built on. Master the four steps here — then apply the same sequence to any specific emotional state through the ten precision modules below.

The Scientific Backbone

Each of the six core voices below maps onto a specific step of the Four-Step Protocol, and each is cited directly inside the resource library for the protocols they inform.

SP

Dr. Stephen Porges

Polyvagal Theory · Neuroscientist

The nervous system has three states — safety, mobilisation, and shutdown — and higher cognitive functions are unavailable while a person is in a survival state. The body has to be signalled toward safety first, through breath, tone, and a soft gaze, before reasoning becomes accessible again.

The Founder

The story is
the product.

The SafeRise Protocol did not emerge from academic study. It emerged from lived navigation — of abandonment trauma, relational patterns that repeated until they were understood, and the long process of learning to recalibrate from survival into grounded, secure presence.

The four-step Protocol was not designed in theory. It was discovered in practice, refined through repetition, and validated through the shift it produced.

When I recognised that every reactive behaviour I carried was rooted in a safety deficit — not a character flaw — everything shifted.

That recognition is what the SafeRise Protocol is built to give others.
